newsitem.title: USA: NASDAQ SHAKES OFF BLUE CHIP SLUMP TO END HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: NASDAQ SHAKES OFF BLUE CHIP SLUMP TO END HIGHER.

text.p: Nasdaq shares finished a choppy and volatile stock market session with slender gains on Wednesday, snapping a streak of losses as gains in Applied Materials Inc lifted semiconductor equipment stocks.

The Nasdaq composite rose 7.16 points, or 0.45 percent, to finish unofficially at 1583.40. Early in the session, it erased gains after a rally in stocks and bonds, sparked by benign July retail and price data, sputtered.
"Most of the nervousness in the Nasdaq market happened before the open," one trader said. "Then, it acted pretty well considering the action by the Dow."
U.S. blue chips closed lower after being whipsawed much of the trading day by bond market swings and a weaker dollar.

Tony Cecin, director of equity trading at Piper Jaffray, said the Nasdaq market recouped some ground from Tuesday's declines, but there was still uncertainty in the market, given the bonds' recent gyrations.
Applied Materials helped buoy the shares of semiconductor equipment makers after it reported stronger-than-expected earnings late Tuesday. It closed up 9-1/8 at 99-3/8.
"Applied Materials is a big technnology supplier, so that helped today," one trader said.
